mechanism.name: post-quantization AF3 objective
mechanism.question: Does optimising the structure of the HARD-SID-induced graph, rather than the continuous embedding, change what the three tokens encode?
mechanism.one_sentence: The geometry is frozen and the objective is not: the edge AF3 target and neighbour retention are read off the quantized readout through a differentiable substitute and returned to the encoder and both codebooks.
mechanism.distinct_from: M1 learns the curvature, M2 learns a radial coordinate, G/L reweight the distance, A supervises the continuous embedding. None of those reads the quantized codes.

computations.statement: phi(q) = [sum_l P_l C_l^E , compose_{l=1..3}(P_l C_l^H)] with the composition right-nested in the ball; it equals the exported hard readout when P is one-hot.
delta_ij = ||phi_i^E - phi_j^E||^2 + d_c(exp_0 phi_i^H, exp_0 phi_j^H)^2 / 4
p_ij = 1 / (1 + exp(delta_ij/tau - b)), with (tau, b) the frozen af3_structure.calibrate pair of one TRAIN snapshot.

F_hat_ij = p_ij [2 - sum_{k != i,j}(p_ik + p_jk) + 3 sum_{k != i,j} p_ik p_jk], the expectation of 4 - d_i - d_j + 3 T_ij under independent Bernoulli edges; the sums run over the anchor's fixed local candidate set.
computations.approximation: The full sums are O(N^2) per anchor; the candidate set is the anchor's TRAIN neighbours plus a fixed sample of TRAIN non-neighbours. The bias against a dense oracle is measured in tests/test_math.py.

computations.statement: L = L_RQ + s [ w_af3 Huber((F_hat - F)/scale) + w_n L_N + w_use L_use ], with L_N the logistic ranking of TRAIN edges above TRAIN non-edges on the fixed support and L_use the mean per-level deficit from a uniform code distribution.

inputs.graph: the canonical TRAIN behaviour graph via tools.research.science.community_curvature.data.build_graph('train'), AF3 F_ij = 4 - d_i - d_j + 3 T_ij from results/research/issue121/community_curvature/train_edge_af3.npz

outputs.sid: three tokens per item, exported as results/stage2_RQ-VAE/TIGER_M4_post_sid_af3/item_sids.json plus the deterministic disambiguation token
outputs.geometry: unchanged: E16 x H16 joint codewords, curvature 1, native residual, the baseline assignment rule including Sinkhorn at the last level

frozen.calibration: tau and b from af3_structure.calibrate on one TRAIN snapshot, written to results/research/issue143/post_calibration.json and reused

parameters.derivation: The three weights are unit weights; the scale that makes them comparable to L_RQ is the gradient-share bound, which is the repository's existing frozen protocol (af3_hierarchy.GradientBudget). No value is chosen by looking at a result.

dimensions.candidate_matrix: anchors x candidates = 96 x 32, never N x N

gradient_rules.encoder: through the soft readout of every level
gradient_rules.codebooks: through P_l C_l, both halves, gradient_norm measured per step
gradient_rules.scale: GradientBudget caps the new terms' combined encoder and codebook gradient at GRADIENT_SHARE of L_RQ's; the minimum over ranks is broadcast, so DDP stays consistent
gradient_rules.kappa: not applicable: the geometry is frozen in this mechanism

training_integration.records: results/stage2_RQ-VAE/TIGER_M4_post_sid_af3/logs/training_metrics.jsonl, including a post_sid event per epoch with the scale and both gradient norms

conventions.distance: d_0(x,y) = 2||x - y||, so d^2/4 is the squared Euclidean distance and the mixed cost at alpha = 1/2 is the plain 32-dimensional squared distance
conventions.readout: right-nested Mobius composition of the three tangent halves, as exported
conventions.sign: AF3 is larger for structurally closer pairs, so a smaller delta must give a larger p; the Huber residual is (F_hat - F)/scale

switches.BEHAVIOUR_ON: the post-SID AF3, retention and usage terms; off => L = L_RQ with the same geometry
switches.GEOMETRY_ON: the curvature of the mixed space; off => CURVATURE = 0 and both halves are Euclidean
switches.policy: the switches exist and are wired; no arm with a switch off is trained (CLAUDE.md 19g)

excluded.reason: discrete; the rule is the baseline's and carries no gradient
a discrete balancing iteration; it is not differentiated
a deterministic discrete sampling of the fixed support; it is not a differentiable quantity
computes once on a frozen snapshot and is then a constant

continuous_surface.note: The edge-level term of the post-SID objective. The local sums of F_hat and the retention and usage terms are additional differentiable terms of the same objective; they are exercised by tests/test_gradient.py because their shape depends on the candidate set, which is not a symbolic argument.
